stem:
Meera sprays perfume in one corner of her classroom in Jaipur. Within a few minutes, Ravi, sitting at the far end, can smell it.

Four students explain why the perfume gas has no fixed shape or fixed volume.

| student | P | Q | R | S |
| explanation | gas particles attract each other strongly and stay in fixed positions | gas particles move freely in all directions with negligible attraction between them | gas particles are far apart but move only in one fixed direction | gas particles move freely and spread out to fill all the available space |

teacher.key_rationale: A gas has no fixed shape or volume because its particles move freely in all directions with negligible interparticle attraction, so they spread to fill the available space. Student Q states free motion with negligible attraction, and student S states free movement filling available space; both correctly explain the property. P wrongly claims strong attraction and fixed positions (solid-like), and R restricts motion to one direction, which would not fill the whole room. Hence Q and S, option B.
